entries.label: Real discount rate for the productivity net present value, with sensitivity rates

citation.title: Cost Benefit Analysis (guidance note)
citation.publisher: Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, July 2023 (marked as under review)

entries.quote: OIA requires the calculation of net present values at an annual real discount rate of 7 per cent. … in addition to the 7 per cent ‘central’ discount rate, the net present values should also be calculated with real discount rates of 3 per cent and 10 per cent.
entries.derivation: Value = the required central rate (7%); low and high = the required sensitivity rates (3% and 10%), reported side by side, not sampled.
entries.notes: An OIA requirement (method "rule", A-P16), matching the brief's defaults (AnalysisSchema: discountRate 0.07, sensitivityRates 0.03 and 0.1). The regulatory burden estimate itself stays undiscounted (RBM p. 6). The guidance note dates from July 2023 and is listed as under review; the OIA also accepts a central 8% (p. 10, footnote 5).

entries.label: IA threshold 2: indicative annual impact on economic and social outcomes

citation.title: Australian Government Impact Analysis Framework: Practical Guide for Agencies
citation.publisher: Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, 1 July 2026
citation.locator: p. 8, 'Preliminary analysis of material economic and social impacts (IA threshold 2)'

entries.quote: IA threshold 2 covers proposals likely to have indicative impacts of $200 million or more a year on economic and social outcomes for people, businesses or community organisations. … This includes, for example, changes in economic growth, household income, investment, innovation and productivity.
entries.derivation: Value = the threshold ($200 million a year). Fixed: a rule.
entries.notes: Used by the evidence gate (F-G-01) and the threshold 2 check (PR-03): the central and low annual GDP effects are compared with it.

entries.label: Range given to a parameter whose source publishes none
entries.units: share of the central value on either side (0.5 = ±50%)

citation.title: Forward plan: prospective policy costing in ALICIA

entries.quote: Every parameter has low, central and high values (from the source's own range or confidence interval; otherwise ±50%, graded D).
entries.derivation: The plan's rule: low = value − 50% of |value|, high = value + 50% of |value|. Entries using it have rangeBasis "plusMinus50".
entries.notes: The tool's assumption, graded D: no source sets the width. The library reads "graded D" as applying to the range, not to the central value, which keeps the grade of its source (A-P15). Four entries use it: c2.r.pc2025-net-zero, c3.sigma.cfm2011 and the two BGVR elasticities (c9.epsilon-*), whose sources give point values only.

entries.label: Realisation factor applied to every productivity effect
entries.units: multiplier (1 = effects as estimated; the user may set 0 to 2)

citation.title: Forward plan: prospective policy costing in ALICIA

entries.derivation: The plan's default (1.0). Fixed: the user sets it (brief AnalysisSchema.realisationFactor, 0 to 2); it is not sampled.
entries.notes: The tool's assumption, graded D. The history of the 1995 NCP reforms (entry general.realisation.ncp-history.pc2024) suggests ex post gains can be less than half the ex ante projection, which a user can apply as a sensitivity.

entries.label: Ratio of the ex post to the ex ante estimate of the 1995 National Competition Policy reforms (sensitivity)

citation.title: National Competition Policy: modelling proposed reforms (study report with appendices)

entries.quote: whereas the Industry Commission (1995) estimated a boost to GDP of up to 5.5% ($23 billion in 1993-94 dollars), the revised estimates a decade later – once reform details and implementation approaches were evident – were less than half that, at 2.5% of GDP ($20 billion presumably in 2003-04 dollars) (PC 2005b).
entries.notes: Not strictly comparable: the 2005 estimate covers observed changes in seven infrastructure sectors and includes the effects of non-NCP factors (plan §6.4). Both are CGE model results.
